Why split
- The supplied proof (Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1); class 𝒯, chapter-07.txt lines 443–486) is the largest of the blowup_class children: 9 preliminaries (P1–P9) and 4 cases (PS-i, PS-ii, ZS-i, ZS-ii), about 23k characters.
- Left atomic, it would need about 300 Lean lines: assembly ≈130, child content ≈90, and ≈75 more to re-prove the localization and vanishing of rescaled integrals. That is about 2.4× the largest sibling formalized in one piece.
- Four steps are self-contained, generic obligations, and the proof uses each of them twice. One more is already accepted elsewhere.

The children
- zero_imrep (P4): the empty IMRep represents the zero current of ℝ^P and has zero weight. It gives 0 ∈ 𝓜 in PS-ii and ZS-ii.
- uniform_mass_bound (P8): monotonicity on B̄_{2r}(z) plus M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ≠ ∞ give δ, Γ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all b ∈ B̄_r(z), x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and ρ < δ. This is the mass hypothesis of (IBL) in ZS-i and ZS-ii.
- zero_scale_iterate: (IBL) plus a tail argument turn every weak limit C of blowUp S y s_k (with S a zero-scale limit and ‖y‖ < 1) into a zero-scale limit of blow-ups of T. This is the 'ν ∈ 𝓜' step of ZS-i (C a tangent cone) and ZS-ii (C = 0).
- weight_convergence (P7 + MassMeasuresConverge): by (BUI), the IMRep weights of blowUp A a s_j equal ofReal(s_j⁻ⁿ)•R.measure.map(dilation a s_j). Mass-measure convergence then gives their vague convergence. This is the convergence step of PS-i (A = T) and ZS-i (A = S).
- blowup_integrals (reused, accepted):
  - (a) eventual localization ∫f d(μ⌞G)^{p,λ_j} = ∫f dμ^{p,λ_j}, used in PS-i in place of the P2/P3 computation;
  - (b) eventual vanishing when μ(B_ε(p)) = 0, used in PS-ii (μ = μ_T⌞W) and ZS-ii (μ = RS.measure).
- The new children take (IBL) and (BUI) as verbatim hypotheses, so none needs an unaccepted declaration.

- A 15-line constant-centre membership step: if dist(p,z) < r and blowUp T p s_j ⇀ C, then the weight of C lies in 𝓜 (tail with s_j < r − dist(p,z)).
- Case PS: p = a+t•y has dist(p,z) < r, and ambient_calculus (7) gives μ^{y,s} = (μ_T⌞W)^{p,ts}.
  - PS-i: (TAN) at p, then constant-centre membership, homogeneity from (TAN), and convergence from blowup_integrals (a) plus weight_convergence.
  - PS-ii: vanishing_blowup and (IM)(a) give a null ball; 0 ∈ 𝓜 by constant-centre membership with R_∅; convergence from blowup_integrals (b).
- Case ZS: dist(b,z) ≤ r, and zero_limit_minimizing applies.
  - ZS-i: (TAN) for S with U = N = univ (ambient_calculus (1)); convergence from weight_convergence; membership from zero_scale_iterate.
  - ZS-ii: vanishing_blowup and (IM)(a) for S; membership from zero_scale_iterate with C = 0; convergence from blowup_integrals (b).

subproblems.title: The zero current in ℝ^P is represented by the empty IMRep, whose weight is the zero measure (preliminary P4)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity representation R of the zero current of ℝ^P: an IMRep R in univ ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P (IMRep univ n) with R.Represents (0 : GeometricCurrentOn univ n), i.e. 0(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_{R.carrier} R.mult·⟨ω, R.orient⟩ dHⁿ for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), and whose weight R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity R.mult is the zero measure. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents (0 : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) ∧ R.measure = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P4 ('the zero member') of the parent's supplied proof, used there in cases (PS-ii) and (ZS-ii) to show 0 ∈ 𝓜. Simon treats the zero current as the integer multiplicity current τ(∅, θ, ξ) (Ch. 6, 3.1).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Euclid P.
1. (The triple.) Let R_∅ have carrier ∅, multiplicity θ :≡ 0 and orientation ξ :≡ 0 (the zero n-vector). We check the fields of IMRep univ n.
 (a) ∅ is a Borel set (MeasurableSet.empty) and ∅ ⊆ univ.
 (b) ∅ is countably n-rectifiable: Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (measure_empty), and every Hⁿ-null set is countably n-rectifiable (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero: the null set itself is the exceptional set M₀ of Definition 1.1).
 (c) θ is constant, hence measurable. The positivity condition 'θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ ∅' is vacuous.
 (d) For every compact K ⊆ univ, ∅ ∩ K = ∅ and Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty), so ∫⁻_{∅∩K} θ dHⁿ = ∫⁻ θ d0 = 0 ≠ ∞ (lintegral_zero_measure).
 (e) ξ is constant, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞∅ (aestronglyMeasurable_const).
 (f) The orientation condition is required only Hⁿ⌞∅-almost everywhere. Since Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, its almost-everywhere filter is ⊥ (ae_zero), so every property, in particular this one, holds a.e.
 Hence R_∅ is an IMRep in univ.
2. (R_∅ represents 0.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be a test form. By definition R_∅.action ω = ∫_{x∈∅} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ = ∫ … d(Hⁿ⌞∅) = ∫ … d0 = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty, integral_zero_measure). The zero current satisfies 0(ω) = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply). Hence 0(ω) = R_∅.action ω for every ω, i.e. R_∅.Represents 0.
3. (Zero weight.) R_∅.measure = (Hⁿ⌞∅).withDensity θ = (0 : Measure).withDensity θ. For every Borel set s, withDensity_apply gives (0).withDensity θ (s) = ∫⁻_s θ d0 = 0 = 0(s). Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext), so R_∅.measure = 0.
Steps 1–3 show that R := R_∅ has the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0; every IMRep field holds because Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (rectifiability by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, a.e. conditions by ae_zero).
Its action is an integral against the zero measure, so it equals 0 = 0(ω); hence it represents the zero current of ℝ^P.
Its weight is a density against the zero measure, so R.measure = 0 (Measure.ext with withDensity_apply).

subproblems.title: Monotonicity on B̄_{2r}(z) and finite mass of B_{2r}(z) give M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ Γρⁿ uniformly near B̄_r(z) (preliminary P8, the mass hypothesis of (IBL))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), z ∈ ℝ^P and r, Λ ∈ ℝ with r > 0 and Λ ≥ 0. Assume: (a) for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z), the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (values in [0, ∞]) is monotone on the open interval (0, R); (b) M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ≠ ∞. Then there are δ > 0 and Γ ∈ ℝ such that M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γ·ρⁿ) for every b ∈ B̄_r(z), every x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and every ρ with 0 < ρ < δ. Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞] is Simon's local mass, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, B_ρ(y) is the open and B̄_R(y) the closed ball.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (z : Euclid P) (r Λ : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ Λ → (∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), closedBall y R ⊆ closedBall z (2 * r) → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) → T.massOn (ball z (2 * r)) ≠ ∞ → ∃ δ Γ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ b ∈ closedBall z r, ∀ x' ∈ ball b δ, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → T.massOn (ball x' ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Γ * ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P8 of the parent's supplied proof (the mass hypothesis of (IBL) at a point b ∈ B̄_r(z)). There, (MON)(i) on the compact set K = B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U supplies the monotonicity (a), and P1 ((IM)(a) and the local integrability of the multiplicity of RT) supplies the finiteness (b). In this child (a) and (b) are hypotheses. The comparison M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T), which P8 obtains from the weight μ_T, is obtained here from the monotonicity of the local mass in the set: M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean covector norm (covectorEuclideanNorm) ≤ 1 at every point, so W₁ ⊆ W₂ implies M_{W₁}(T) ≤ M_{W₂}(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono, SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. (Constants.) Put Γ′ := ofReal(e^{Λ·(r/4)}/(r/4)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ∈ [0, ∞]. Since ofReal(·) ≠ ∞ and M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ≠ ∞ by (b), Γ′ ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). Put δ := r/4 > 0 and Γ := Γ′.toReal ≥ 0. Note that δ and Γ do not depend on b.
2. (Geometry.) Let b ∈ B̄_r(z), x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Then dist(x′, z) ≤ dist(x′, b) + dist(b, z) < r/4 + r = 5r/4. Consequently:
 (i) B̄_{r/2}(x′) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z): if dist(w, x′) ≤ r/2 then dist(w, z) ≤ dist(w, x′) + dist(x′, z) < r/2 + 5r/4 = 7r/4 ≤ 2r;
 (ii) B_{r/4}(x′) ⊆ B_{2r}(z): if dist(w, x′) < r/4 then dist(w, z) < r/4 + 5r/4 = 3r/2 < 2r.
3. (Monotonicity.) By (i), hypothesis (a) applies with (y, R) := (x′, r/2): the function f(τ) := ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τⁿ)·M_{B_τ(x′)}(T) is monotone on (0, r/2). Both ρ and r/4 lie in (0, r/2), and ρ ≤ r/4 (indeed ρ < δ = r/4). Hence f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4).
4. (Bound at radius r/4.) By (ii) and the monotonicity of the local mass in the set, M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T). Multiplying by ofReal(e^{Λ(r/4)}/(r/4)ⁿ) gives f(r/4) ≤ Γ′.
5. (Removing the exponential.) Since Λ ≥ 0 and ρ > 0 we have Λρ ≥ 0, so e^{Λρ} ≥ 1 (Real.one_le_exp). Dividing by ρⁿ > 0 gives 1/ρⁿ ≤ e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ, hence ofReal(1/ρⁿ) ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), and therefore ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4) ≤ Γ′ by steps 3 and 4.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ρⁿ > 0, ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(1/ρⁿ) = ofReal(ρⁿ·(1/ρⁿ)) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence
 M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) = ofReal(ρⁿ)·(ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T)) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ (step 5).
 As Γ′ ≠ ∞, Γ′ = ofReal(Γ′.toReal) = ofReal(Γ) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), so ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ = ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(Γ) = ofReal(Γ·ρⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ρⁿ ≥ 0).
 Thus M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all b ∈ B̄_r(z), x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take δ := r/4 and Γ := (ofReal(e^{Λr/4}/(r/4)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T)).toReal, finite by (b).
For b ∈ B̄_r(z) and x′ ∈ B_{r/4}(b): dist(x′, z) < 5r/4, so B̄_{r/2}(x′) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z) and B_{r/4}(x′) ⊆ B_{2r}(z).
Monotonicity on (0, r/2) gives f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4), and f(r/4) ≤ Γ′ because the local mass is monotone in the set.
e^{Λρ} ≥ 1 removes the exponential; multiplying by ofReal(ρⁿ) gives M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ = ofReal(Γρⁿ).

subproblems.title: Iterated blow-ups of a zero-scale limit at a point of the unit ball are again zero-scale limits of blow-ups of T (the (IBL) membership step)
subproblems.statement: Assume (IBL) — verbatim the frozen type of the registered dependency iterated_blowup_limit of the grandparent node blowup_class: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ U, x_i → x, λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), y ∈ ℝ^P, s_k > 0 with s_k → 0 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): if there are δ > 0 and Γ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(x) and 0 < ρ < δ, blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly), then there is a strictly increasing φ with blowUp T (x_{φ(k)} + λ_{φ(k)}•y) (λ_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), z ∈ ℝ^P, r ∈ ℝ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), points c_i ∈ ℝ^P and scales t_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), and b ∈ U, such that dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i for every i, t_i → 0, c_i → b, blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), and there are δ > 0 and Γ ∈ ℝ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Let y ∈ ℝ^P with ‖y‖ < 1, s_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) with s_k → 0, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. Then there are points c′_k ∈ ℝ^P and scales t′_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) such that dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k for every k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.

Source: the class-membership step 'ν ∈ 𝓜' of cases (ZS-i) and (ZS-ii) of the parent's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), chapter-07.txt lines 443–486: a tangent cone of a member of 𝒯₀ is again in 𝒯₀ because η_{y,s#}η_{x_i,λ_i#}T = η_{x_i+λ_iy, λ_is#}T). Here C is arbitrary; in the parent C is a tangent cone of S at y, or the zero current.
1. (Iterated limit.) Apply (IBL) with P, n, U (open), T, x := b ∈ U, xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i) (positive), S, y, ss := (s_k) (positive) and C. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumptions: c_i → b, t_i → 0, s_k → 0, the mass bound at b with (δ, Γ), blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. It gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C.
2. (A tail with small scales.) Since ‖y‖ < 1, the number 1 − ‖y‖ is positive, so {s ∈ ℝ : s < 1 − ‖y‖} is a neighbourhood of 0. As s_k → 0, there is k₀ ∈ ℕ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀.
3. (New data.) For k ∈ ℕ put i(k) := φ(k + k₀), c′_k := c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y and t′_k := t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀}. Then t′_k > 0 as a product of two positive numbers.
4. (The admissibility inequality.) Fix k. Since t_{i(k)} > 0, dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) = ‖t_{i(k)}•y‖ = t_{i(k)}‖y‖. By the triangle inequality and the assumption dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < r − t_{i(k)},
 dist(c′_k, z) ≤ dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) + dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < t_{i(k)}‖y‖ + r − t_{i(k)} = r − t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖).
 Since k + k₀ ≥ k₀, step 2 gives s_{k+k₀} < 1 − ‖y‖, so t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖) > t_{i(k)}s_{k+k₀} = t′_k (t_{i(k)} > 0). Hence dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k.
5. (Limits of the data.) The map k ↦ k + k₀ tends to ∞ (tendsto_add_atTop_nat), and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ tends to ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop); hence i(k) → ∞. Therefore t_{i(k)} → 0, c_{i(k)} → b and s_{k+k₀} → 0. It follows that t′_k = t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀} → 0·0 = 0 (Tendsto.mul) and c′_k = c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y → b + 0•y = b (Tendsto.add, Tendsto.smul_const).
6. (Weak convergence.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be a test form. By step 1, currentEval(blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k)) ω → C(ω). Composing this real sequence with k ↦ k + k₀ (which tends to ∞) gives a sequence with the same limit, and its k-th term is currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω: the centres and scales agree, and the proofs of nonvanishing of the scale inside blowUp are irrelevant (proof irrelevance). Hence currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω → C(ω) for every ω, i.e. blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.
Steps 3–6 show that (c′_k), (t′_k) satisfy all requirements: t′_k > 0, dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: (IBL) at x := b with the data (c_i, t_i), S, y, (s_k), C gives a strictly increasing φ with blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C.
Choose k₀ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀ (s_k → 0 and ‖y‖ < 1).
Put c′_k := c_{φ(k+k₀)} + t_{φ(k+k₀)}y and t′_k := t_{φ(k+k₀)}s_{k+k₀} > 0; the triangle inequality gives dist(c′_k, z) < r − t_{φ(k+k₀)}(1 − ‖y‖) < r − t′_k.
t′_k → 0 and c′_k → b, and the tail k ↦ k + k₀ of the weakly convergent sequence of step 1 converges weakly to C.

subproblems.title: Along blow-ups with mass-measure convergence, the rescaled IMRep weights converge vaguely to the weight of the limit (preliminary P7 with MassMeasuresConverge)
subproblems.statement: Assume (BUI) — verbatim the frozen type of the registered dependency blowup_imrep of the grandparent node blowup_class (the reused accepted rep_pushforward): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and every IMRep R of T in U there is an IMRep R′ in dilation x λ '' U representing blowUp T x λ with R′.measure(s) = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure((dilation x λ)⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n) with an IMRep R of A in V (R.Represents A), a ∈ ℝ^P, scales s_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ), and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with an IMRep R_C of C in ℝ^P. Suppose MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp A a s_j) C. Then for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, ∫ f d(ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j)) → ∫ f dR_C.measure as j → ∞, where dilation a s (v) = s⁻¹(v − a).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P7 (IMReps of blow-ups and their weights) of the parent's supplied proof, together with the use of MassMeasuresConverge in the convergence steps of cases (PS-i) (A := T, R := RT, a := p, s_j := tλ_{φ(j)}) and (ZS-i) (A := S, R := RS, a := y, s_j := λ_{φ(j)}).
Notation: η_j := dilation a s_j, so η_j(v) = −(s_j⁻¹•a) + s_j⁻¹•v = s_j⁻¹(v − a); m_j := ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map η_j.
1. (Measurability of the dilations.) For every s ∈ ℝ, dilation a s is v ↦ −(s⁻¹•a) + dilationCLM P s v, the sum of a constant and a continuous linear map. Hence it is continuous and therefore Borel measurable.
2. (IMReps of the blow-ups.) For each j, apply (BUI) to (P, n, V, A, a, s_j > 0, R), using R.Represents A. It gives an IMRep R_j in dilation a s_j '' V with R_j.Represents (blowUp A a s_j) and R_j.measure(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) for every Borel set B. Choose one such R_j for every j ∈ ℕ (axiom of choice).
3. (Their weights are the rescaled measures.) Let j ∈ ℕ and let B be Borel. By the definition of the scalar multiple of a measure and of the push-forward (Measure.smul_apply; Measure.map_apply, which applies because η_j is measurable by step 1 and B is Borel),
 m_j(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·(R.measure.map η_j)(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) = R_j.measure(B) (step 2).
 Measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext), so R_j.measure = m_j for every j.
4. (Mass-measure convergence.) By definition, MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp A a s_j) C says: for every family of IMReps of the blow-ups (one in each domain dilation a s_j '' V), every IMRep of C in ℝ^P and every continuous compactly supported f with tsupport f ⊆ ℝ^P, the integrals of f against the weights converge. Apply it to the family (R_j) of step 2, to R_C, to f and to tsupport f ⊆ ℝ^P = univ. This gives ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dR_C.measure as j → ∞.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 3, ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫ f dm_j for every j. Hence ∫ f d(ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j)) → ∫ f dR_C.measure. ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation a s is an affine map with continuous linear part, hence continuous and measurable.
(BUI) gives, for every j, an IMRep R_j of blowUp A a s_j whose weight is B ↦ ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure((dilation a s_j)⁻¹(B)); choose them for all j.
Measure.ext with Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply: R_j.measure = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j).
MassMeasuresConverge applied to (R_j), R_C, f and tsupport f ⊆ univ gives the convergence of ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫ f d(rescaled weight) to ∫ f dR_C.measure.

subproblems.title: Blow-up integrals of compactly supported functions: eventual localization to an open neighbourhood, and eventual vanishing at a null ball (parent steps 1–2) (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For a measure ν on ℝ^P, a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0, write ν^{a,s} := ofReal(s^{−n})•ν.map(dilation a s), where dilation a s (y) = s⁻¹(y − a). Let λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ) with λ_j → 0, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ have compact support. No continuity or integrability of f is assumed; integrals are Bochner integrals. (a) If μ is a measure on ℝ^P, G ⊆ ℝ^P is open and p ∈ G, then ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,λ_j} = ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} for all sufficiently large j. (b) If μ is a measure on ℝ^P, p ∈ ℝ^P, ε > 0 and μ(B_ε(p)) = 0, then ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} = 0 for all sufficiently large j.

Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.idtp_fons_cc_tm_blowup_integrals (DAG node …cone_class-a1.tangent_measures-a1.blowup_integrals-a1 of the flat_off_null_set branch, status accepted, candidate commit 926c111dd53ee0c9413099cd843d15fd58a6cc4d, isolated comparator passed). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use under the selected node: part (a) is the localization step of case (PS-i) (with μ := μ_T = RT.measure, G := B_{2r}(z), p := a + t•y and scales tλ_{φ(j)}), which replaces the P2/P3 computation ∫ f∘η d(μ_T⌞W) = ∫ f∘η dμ_T of the supplied proof; part (b) is the vanishing step of cases (PS-ii) (μ := μ_T⌞B_{2r}(z), the null ball B_ε(p), scales tλ_j) and (ZS-ii) (μ := RS.measure, the null ball B_ε(y), scales λ_j). The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent'/'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: parent proof step 1 (localization: (μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η_{p,s}(G) ⊇ B_{δ/s}(0), and tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/λ_j}(0) for large j) and step 2 (a null ball B_ε(p) makes the blow-up integrals eventually 0). The parent proof takes these dilation facts from its sibling ambient_calculus (items (2), (3), (4), (9)); they are proved directly here.
Notation: for a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0, η := dilation a s, so η(y) = −s⁻¹a + s⁻¹y = s⁻¹(y − a). Write c_s := ofReal((s)⁻¹ ^ n).
1. (η is a homeomorphism.) For s ≠ 0, η is the composition of y ↦ s⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero) and z ↦ −s⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft). Hence η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P and so a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding); in particular it is injective and measurable. It is surjective: η(a + s z) = z for every z.
2. (Balls.) Let s > 0. Then η(y) = s⁻¹(y − a), so ‖η(y)‖ = |s⁻¹|·‖y − a‖ = ‖y − a‖/s. Hence, for every r ∈ ℝ, η⁻¹(B_r(0)) = {y : ‖y − a‖/s < r} = {y : ‖y − a‖ < s r} = B_{s r}(a). Since η is surjective, B_r(0) = η(η⁻¹(B_r(0))) = η(B_{s r}(a)). With r = δ/s this gives B_{δ/s}(0) = η(B_δ(a)) for every δ, since s·(δ/s) = δ.
3. (Eventual containment of the support.) Let r > 0. Since tsupport f is compact, it is bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 M for some M ∈ ℝ. Since λ_j > 0 for all j and λ_j → 0, λ_j → 0 within (0, ∞) (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Hence λ_j⁻¹ → +∞ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero), and r/λ_j = r·λ_j⁻¹ → +∞ (Tendsto.const_mul_atTop, r > 0). So r/λ_j > M for all large j, and then tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 M ⊆ B_{r/λ_j}(0) (closedBall_subset_ball).
4. (Proof of (a).) G is open and p ∈ G, so there is δ > 0 with B_δ(p) ⊆ G (Metric.isOpen_iff). By step 3 with r := δ, tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/λ_j}(0) for all large j. Fix such a j and put s := λ_j > 0 and η := dilation p s.
 (i) (Restriction commutes with the blow-up.) Since η is a measurable embedding, (μ.map η)⌞η(G) = (μ⌞η⁻¹(η(G))).map η (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map), and η⁻¹(η(G)) = G by injectivity (preimage_image_eq). Multiply by the scalar c_s and use (c•ν)⌞B = c•(ν⌞B) (Measure.restrict_smul). This gives c_s•(μ⌞G).map η = (c_s•μ.map η)⌞η(G), i.e. (μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η(G). Hence ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,s} = ∫_{η(G)} f dμ^{p,s}.
 (ii) (f vanishes off η(G).) Let x ∉ η(G) and suppose f(x) ≠ 0. Then x ∈ support f ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ B_{δ/s}(0). By step 2 with a := p, B_{δ/s}(0) = η(B_δ(p)) ⊆ η(G), because B_δ(p) ⊆ G. This contradicts x ∉ η(G). So f(x) = 0 for every x ∉ η(G).
 (iii) By (ii), ∫_{η(G)} f dμ^{p,s} = ∫ f dμ^{p,s} (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, which needs no measurability or integrability hypothesis). With (i), ∫ f d(μ⌞G)^{p,λ_j} = ∫ f dμ^{p,λ_j} for all large j, which is (a).
5. (Proof of (b).) By step 3 with r := ε, tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/λ_j}(0) for all large j. Fix such j and put s := λ_j > 0 and η := dilation p s.
 (i) (The ball is null.) B_{ε/s}(0) is measurable and η is measurable. So μ^{p,s}(B_{ε/s}(0)) = c_s·(μ.map η)(B_{ε/s}(0)) = c_s·μ(η⁻¹(B_{ε/s}(0))) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply). By step 2 this equals c_s·μ(B_{s·(ε/s)}(p)) = c_s·μ(B_ε(p)) = c_s·0 = 0.
 (ii) {x : f(x) ≠ 0} = support f ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/s}(0), so this set is μ^{p,s}-null (measure_mono_null). That is, f = 0 μ^{p,s}-almost everywhere (ae_iff). Hence ∫ f dμ^{p,s} = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
 This holds for all large j, which is (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation a s (s > 0) is a surjective homeomorphism (a measurable embedding) with η⁻¹(B_r(0)) = B_{sr}(a) and η(B_δ(a)) = B_{δ/s}(0).
tsupport f is bounded and r/λ_j → +∞, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{r/λ_j}(0) for all large j.
(μ⌞G)^{p,s} = (μ^{p,s})⌞η(G) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, Measure.restrict_smul). For large j, f vanishes off η(G) ⊇ η(B_δ(p)) = B_{δ/s}(0), so the two integrals agree.
μ^{p,s}(B_{ε/s}(0)) = ofReal(s^{−n})·μ(B_ε(p)) = 0, so for large j, f = 0 μ^{p,s}-a.e. and ∫ f dμ^{p,s} = 0.
